title: How learnc lint checks a lesson

source.content:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Author
  participant L as Lint CLI
  participant C as Compiler
  A->>L: Run learnc lint
  L->>C: Validate and resolve
  C-->>L: Frozen lesson
  L-->>A: Findings and exit status

highlights.annotation: Policy starts only after compilation succeeds; it reads the same in-memory artifact that `check` would discard.
The rule pass receives both authored structure and frozen content, while source spans stay separate from the artifact.

prompt.content: Why does `learnc lint` compile before running its policy rules?

choices.content: So rules inspect resolved, validated lesson content.
So rules can rewrite source files before the build.
So rules can assign learner progress identifiers.

hints: Consider which data the rules use and what happens when compilation fails.
blocks.explanation: Compilation establishes a trustworthy, frozen view of the lesson. A failure stops lint before authoring-policy rules inspect unreliable input.

prompt.content: Which Mermaid condition must stop `learnc check` and `learnc build`?

choices.content: The Rust parser rejects the resolved diagram.
A diagram has no `classDef` legend entries.

hints: Separate parser rejection from an authoring-style warning.
blocks.explanation: The partial Rust syntax gate is a compiler check. Flowchart grouping and styling are lint policy, where intentional exceptions are possible.

prompt.content: Where should a lint finding about content frozen from a Git revision primarily point?

choices.content: The frozen content inside the `.learn` artifact.
The current worktree file with the same path.

hints: The primary location should be something the author can edit to change the lesson.
blocks.explanation: A revision's content is historical and may differ from the current worktree. The lesson's source declaration is the reliable edit target.

highlights.annotation: The set counts each displayed line once, then applies both the minimum-line and coverage-ratio thresholds.

prompt.content: Can a warning hidden by `--ignore-below critical` still make lint exit nonzero?

choices.content: No; filtering happens before fatality is computed.
Yes; any warning is fatal whenever an error also exists.

hints: Look at the order of the filter and map operations in `LintReport`.
blocks.explanation: Suppressed findings never enter the report's fatality calculation. Compiler-validation failures are separate and cannot be suppressed by this flag.

prompt.content: What does an explicit lint TOML file change?

choices.content: Only lint rule thresholds for that invocation.
The source schema accepted by check and build.
The intrinsic severity assigned to every rule.

hints: Distinguish a threshold override from validity or severity.
blocks.explanation: TOML keys override numeric lint thresholds, and matching CLI flags take precedence over TOML. Rule severities stay intrinsic, while `--warning-as-error` controls which reported findings are fatal.
